_about: Mechanical reference geometry for gb2 outlines (drawn by draw_mech.py). Researched 2026-09-28; every item carries its source + confidence. tft: Adafruit 2090 module, frame = module PCB centre, +X toward JP2, +Y down, viewed from the screen side (= KiCad top view). gba: Nintendo Game Boy Advance AGB-001 front view, frame = top-left of the 144.5 x 82 bounding box, +X right, +Y down.

tft.frame: Origin: the centre of the Adafruit 2090 module PCB. This is Eagle board (0,0): the outline is symmetric about it in both Adafruit .brd files. +X points toward the JP2 short edge (the SPI/microSD header, which is also the end where the panel's FPC exits). +Y points down, viewed from the SCREEN (front) side, so the axes are screen coordinates. Units: mm. Mapping from Eagle board coordinates (the Eagle top view is the module's BACK/component side): X = -y_eagle, Y = +x_eagle. This is a pure 90-degree rotation with no mirror. Heights are given as distances along the view axis (+Z points away from the viewer, toward the mainboard). The screen-up module is seen from above, the same way KiCad shows the mainboard top side. So these (X,Y) values drop straight into the mainboard KiCad top view after adding the module-centre offset. Mainboard socket pin n sits directly under module header pin n.

tft.notes:
Checked the BOM rows #15-#17 against Adafruit's own board files, the panel datasheet drawing, and the product page and photos. All the BOM numbers hold, with one correction about the board shape.

- **The board is not a rectangle.** 81.28 x 62.484 mm is only the bounding box. The board is I-shaped:
  - a 71.12 x 50.8 mm centre body (Y within +-25.4)
  - plus a 5.08 mm-wide strip at each short end, X = +-35.56 to +-40.64, extending out to Y = +-31.242 with R2.54 semicircular ends.
  - The inner corners where the strips meet the body are square.
  - **What this frees up:** the regions |Y| 25.4-31.24 with |X| < 35.56 (above and below the panel) are empty of the module. Only the ears reach out to 62.5 mm. The BOM says 'board 81.3 x 62.5 mm' and should add 'I-shape, 50.8 mm wide between the header strips'.
- **Headers.** JP1 is the 8-bit side, at X = -38.1. JP2 is the SPI/microSD side, at X = +38.1; the panel's FPC also exits at this end. They are 76.2 mm apart (verified). Both are R180 in Eagle, so pin 1 (square GND) of both is at Y = +24.13 and pin n is at Y = 24.13 - 2.54(n-1). The product photos confirm this: GND is at the same end on both strips.
- **Mounting holes.** Four 3.0 mm plated drills (pad dia 3.6, silk ring dia 4.4) at (+-38.1, +-28.575). That is a 76.2 x 57.15 mm pattern, in line with the headers (verified). The hole centres sit 0.127 mm inboard of the ear arc centres.
- **Panel position.** The 50 x 69.2 panel is centred at X = +0.16, Y = 0. It spans X -34.44 to +34.76, so it stays inside the centre body with a 0.4 mm inset on the long edges.
  - The active area is offset toward JP1: centre X = -2.64 per the panel spec (3.00 mm border at the JP1 end, 8.60 mm at the FPC end, 3.40 mm on the long sides).
  - Adafruit's Eagle drawing puts it 0.32 mm further toward JP1 (centre X = -2.96). Treat about 0.3 mm as the placement uncertainty.
  - The cover lens (68.75 x 49.5) and the touch viewing area (58.6 x 44.2) are listed separately. Use the viewing area for a bezel window.
  - The product page says 'Screen: 69.6 x 45.2 mm', which matches neither the spec nor the CAD. I did not use it.
- **FPC path.** The FPC exits the panel's JP2 end and wraps around that edge on the front, bulging out at most 1.0 mm (X <= 35.76, still over the JP2 strip, clear of the JP2 pads at X >= 37.26).
  - It then runs flat behind the panel, goes through a milled slot in the module PCB (X 15.75-21.08, Y +-14.99), and is soldered on the module back to a 50-pad row at X = 7.85 (pin 1 at Y = -12.25).
  - The touch-controller chip on the FPC sits recessed in a milled pocket (X 21.08-34.54, Y 5.97-21.97).
  - Nothing of the FPC hangs outside the module outline, and on the mainboard-facing side it is only about 0.3-0.5 mm thick.
  - The spec's FPC length (26.8 unbent, 25.0 bent) is about 2 mm short of what this route needs if the fold is creased flat. The fold is evidently not flat in Adafruit's assembly; this has no effect on the envelope.
- **Heights.** Glass top is about 4.1 mm above the module PCB front (panel 4.0 +-0.2 plus 0.1 tape; allow about 4.4). The module PCB is about 1.57 mm. The module back sits about 11.0 mm above the mainboard: the 8.5 mm socket (LCSC spec) plus a male header body of about 2.5 mm (estimated). So the glass top is about 16.7 mm above the mainboard. All back-side parts are 2.65 mm or less, well within that gap.
- **Two board revisions exist; the geometry above holds for both.** Outline, holes, headers, panel position, slot/pocket and FPC pads are identical in both .brd files. Only the back-side parts differ:
  - Original: two 74LVC245 in SOIC-20W, about 2.65 mm tall.
  - Rev D (Dec 2022): TSSOP-20 about 1.2 mm, an 18-pin EYESPI connector at X -24.9 to -11.9, Y 20.4-24.8, and the microSD socket in the same place.
- **Viewing angle.** This is a TN panel whose best viewing direction ('6 o'clock') points along +X toward JP2. In a landscape handheld, the vertical viewing axis is the symmetric one.
- **Sources.** The Adafruit repo is github.com/adafruit/Adafruit-2.8-TFT-with-Capacitive-Touch-PCB. Its .sch files are the same byte size as cad/docs/adafruit-2090-cap-touch.sch (329748) and -revD.sch (347493), which confirms it is the matching design. The panel drawing is page 5 of cad/docs/SPEC-DT280QV10-CT_Rev.B.pdf; the page-4 table gives the 4.0 mm module thickness.
- **Scratch files in /tmp/gb2-mech/:** orig.brd, revD.brd, top300l.png and mid300l.png (spec drawing crops, rotated), xf.py (coordinate transform), and the product photos 2090-*.jpg.

gba.frame: Front view of the Nintendo Game Boy Advance AGB-001, looking at the screen side with the unit upright and the cartridge slot at the top. Origin (0,0) is the top-left corner of the axis-aligned bounding box of the whole front silhouette, including the shoulder buttons. +x runs right (toward A/B), +y runs down (toward the bottom edge). Units are mm. The bounding box is 144.5 x 82, the vertical centreline is x=72.25, and the bbox mid-height is y=41.0. Where depth is given, it is mm behind the front face, or in front of the rear-most back surface where stated.

items.name: GBA overall bounding box (W x H; depth 24.5)
items.source: Nintendo Japan hardware spec page https://www.nintendo.co.jp/n08/hardware/spec/index.html, GBA column: 寸法 縦82mm×横144.5mm×厚さ24.5mm; 本体重量 約140g (乾電池含まず). The same figures appear in en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_Boy_Advance (infobox and spec table).

items.name: GBA front silhouette outline (52-pt closed polyline, clockwise, L/R symmetric)
items.source: Traced from Nintendo design patent US D452,280 S ('Hand-held electronic game machine', priority 2000-01-21, issued 2001-12-18), FIG.1 front elevation, sheet https://patentimages.storage.googleapis.com/c0/d2/99/33b659ab3127e4/USD0452280-20011218-D00001.png. The drawing's ink bbox (1915 x 1084 px) was scaled to the official 144.5 x 82 (13.25 / 13.22 px/mm). The drawing's aspect is 1.7666 against the spec's 1.7622 (0.25% difference). I filled the outer silhouette, closed the roughly 1 mm parting notches between the L/R buttons and the body (2.3 mm morphological close), averaged the left and right halves (the drawing is symmetric to within 0.3 mm), and simplified with Douglas-Peucker. Maximum deviation from the traced contour is 0.17 mm; area is 10598 mm2.

items.name: Silhouette shape descriptors
items.source: Circle fits to the traced FIG.1 contour (US D452,280). (1) The top is flat at y=0 for x 39.1-105.4. (2) The shoulders fall gently (R about 80 mm, convex) to y=1.7 at x=33.1/111.4 and y=4.0 at x=13.8/130.7. (3) The upper corners are R about 10.0 mm, centred near (14.3,14.4) and (130.2,14.4). (4) The ends are almost straight and flare outward going down, from x=3.55 at y=15.5 to x=0 at y 50-60; the widest point is at y about 51-59. (5) The lower corners are R about 10.6, centred near (10.9,60.2) and (133.6,60.2). (6) There is a small flat at y about 70.45 for x 7.3-10.4 and 134.1-137.2, where the grey corner caps meet the body. (7) The bottom edge is an arc of R about 157 mm, lowest (y=82) at x=72.25 and at y=74.7 at x=25.7/118.8. A 144.5 x 82 rounded rectangle is a poor stand-in, because the bottom bows by about 7 mm and the top corners sit about 4 mm lower than the flat top.

items.name: Screen spec
items.source: Nintendo JP spec page https://www.nintendo.co.jp/n08/hardware/spec/index.html: 反射型TFTカラー液晶 (reflective TFT, no light), 画面サイズ 40.8mm×61.2mm, 解像度 240×160, 32000色. The 2.9-inch figure is from the Nintendo JP GBA page https://www.nintendo.co.jp/n08/hardware/gba/index.html ('2.9インチ反射型TFTカラー液晶'). Check: the diagonal of 61.2 x 40.8 is 73.55 mm = 2.896 in; the pixel pitch is 0.255 mm.

items.name: LCD active area 240x160 (61.2 x 40.8)
items.source: Size is official (Nintendo JP spec page). The centre is taken from the clear-window rectangle in US D452,280 FIG.1: measured centre (71.95, 36.67), with x placed on the unit centreline 72.25, a 0.3 mm shift. That gives an active area of x 41.65-102.85, y 16.27-57.07.

items.name: Screen lens clear window (rectangle as drawn)
items.source: US D452,280 FIG.1: straight window lines found by run-length detection at x 41.01/102.88 and y 15.74/57.60 (line centres), giving 61.9 x 41.9. The window is 0.35 mm (horizontal) and 0.55 mm (vertical) larger than the 61.2 x 40.8 active area on each side, which is consistent with the scale. Measured centre x is 71.95, placed on 72.25.

items.name: Screen lens / bezel outer outline (40-pt closed polyline)
items.source: US D452,280 FIG.1: the lens perimeter line, traced at line centre. The top and bottom edges come from column scans that skip the hatching. The corners come from rays cast out of the window corners. The sides are a quadratic fit to the clean right-hand edge (residual 0.07 mm), mirrored. The lens is symmetric about its own centre (71.97 in the drawing) and was moved onto 72.25. The bbox is 74.5 x 63.5 (x 34.98-109.52, y 9.10-72.58). The top is slightly arched, the top corners are R about 3 mm, the sides lean outward going down (69.7 mm wide at y=15, 74.5 mm at y=58), the bottom corners are R about 7 mm, and the bottom edge bows down to 72.58.

items.name: D-pad centre
items.source: Production AGB-CPU-10 board scan (1200 DPI, github.com/djedditt/kicad-agb-template, scans/AGB-CPU-10_sideA_front.png). The centre is the mean of the gold-pad centroids UP (22.79,26.53), DOWN (22.77,43.76), LEFT (14.09,35.14) and RIGHT (31.37,35.07) in scan mm. Scan scale was corrected by x0.99547, calibrated on the 1.50 mm-pitch cartridge-connector pads (measured pitch 1.5068 over 31 pads). Registration: x = (x_scan - 75.30)*0.99547 + 72.25, because the board's mounting holes are symmetric about x_scan=75.30; y = y_scan*0.99547 - 0.88, a least-squares fit of D-pad/A/B/Start/Select to the patent. The patent FIG.1 centre circle is at (20.11, 34.02).

items.name: D-pad cross cap outline (span 18.8, arm width 6.0)
items.source: Sizes from US D452,280 FIG.1. The cap edges are at x 10.9/29.7 and y 25.0/43.7 (line centres), about 18.8 x 18.7. The arm edges are at x about 17.0/23.1 and y about 31.3/37.0, about 6 mm wide. The shell recess around the cross is about 21.3 mm across (x 9.66-30.94). The cross is centred on the board-derived D-pad centre.

items.name: A button
items.source: Centre: AGB-CPU-10 scan A contact pattern centroid (134.2, 32.95 scan mm), registered as for the D-pad; the patent FIG.1 centre is (130.43, 31.77). Diameter: about 9.4-9.5 mm between line centres in FIG.1 (edges 125.8/135.2 and 27.1/36.6).

items.name: B button
items.source: Centre: AGB-CPU-10 scan B contact centroid (121.2, 37.3 scan mm), registered; the patent FIG.1 centre is (117.45, 36.42). Diameter about 9.2-9.5 (FIG.1). The A-B centre spacing is 13.65 (board) against 13.79 (patent).

items.name: START button (upper)
items.source: Centre: AGB-CPU-10 scan START contact centroid (32.34, 54.95 scan mm), registered; the patent FIG.1 centre is (29.65, 53.90). The cap is about 4.0 mm across and the shell recess about 5 mm (FIG.1 line runs). The embossed 'START' oval runs diagonally to the left, about x 16.7-27, about 13 x 5.5 mm.

items.name: SELECT button (lower)
items.source: Centre: AGB-CPU-10 scan SELECT contact centroid (32.30, 62.99 scan mm), registered; the patent FIG.1 centre is (29.65, 61.80). Cap about 4.0 mm across. The 'SELECT' oval sits about 7.9 mm below the START oval.

items.name: Power LED window
items.source: Centre: the centre of the 2x2 LED pad block DL1/DL2 (red/green) on the AGB-CPU-10 scan (121.4, 15.65 scan mm), registered. The patent FIG.1 window is centred at (117.56, 14.56) with a diameter of about 2.5 mm (edges 116.25/118.73, 13.27/15.88). The 'POWER' legend sits to its right.

items.name: Speaker grille slot 1 (top), centreline
items.source: US D452,280 FIG.1. There are five parallel slots at centre x 120.7 and y 50.67/53.61/56.56/59.52/62.46 (pitch 2.95), tilted 13.7 deg with the right end higher (PCA of the slot outlines). Each slot is about 16.7 long outside and about 1.6 wide outside; the actual opening is about 1 mm. The count of five and the tilt direction match the production photo commons.wikimedia.org File:Game_Boy_Advance_front.jpg.

items.name: Cartridge slot opening (top edge, rear half of thickness)

The 7.5 mm opening matches the Game Pak thickness of 7.5 mm (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_Boy_Game_Pak).

items.source: Cartridge size is 35 tall x 57-58 wide with a 60 mm grip lip at the top (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_Boy_Game_Pak; Nintendo JP GBA page says 縦34.5mm×横60mm). items.name: AGB-CPU-10 production motherboard outline (96-pt polyline, includes battery cut-out)
items.source: github.com/djedditt/kicad-agb-template kicad/AGB_template.kicad_pcb Edge.Cuts, traced from the 1200 DPI scan. The embedded Dwgs.User image is exactly the top 3996 rows of the scan, centred at (151.775, 91.175), so template coordinates minus (76.6965, 48.884) give scan mm. The outline was simplified to 0.4 mm and registered with the same formulas as the D-pad. The board is 130.6 x 72.5 (x 6.85-137.47, y 3.38-75.89) and sits inside the silhouette on all sides.

items.name: Depth budget (thickness vs x, symmetric about 72.25)
items.source: US D452,280 FIG.3 top view (rear-surface profile against the front-face line), with the depth axis normalised so the body is 24.5 (x0.958; the drawing shows 25.6, about 4.5% over-scale in depth). Thickness excluding button caps, mirrored at 144.5-x: x=2 about 10.6; x=5 about 14.5; x=10 about 16.4; x=15 about 18.8; x=20 about 20.8; x=25 about 22.2; x=30 about 23.3; x=35 about 24.0; x=38-106 about 24.5 (the full-depth central band carrying the cartridge housing at top and the battery box at bottom). The FIG.4 bottom view agrees: about 21.3 at x=20, and the battery bump spans x about 40.7-103.5. The D-pad and A/B caps stand about 1.9-2.1 mm proud of the front face; the official 24.5 excludes them. Stack in the central band, front to back: front shell and lens, LCD, PCB, then the cartridge in the rear 1.8-9.3 mm (top half) or the 2xAA box (14.5 mm cells plus door, about 16 mm, bottom half). That leaves roughly 15 mm in front of the cartridge and roughly 8.5 mm in front of the cells for shell + LCD + PCB (estimate).

gba.notes:
All figures are in the frame above. I rendered every item as an overlay and checked it visually.

1. **Official dimensions confirmed.** Nintendo JP's spec page (https://www.nintendo.co.jp/n08/hardware/spec/index.html) gives 縦82 x 横144.5 x 厚さ24.5 mm, about 140 g without batteries, a reflective TFT screen of 40.8 x 61.2 mm at 240x160, and power from 2x AA (about 15 h) or the battery pack. The 2.9-inch figure is on https://www.nintendo.co.jp/n08/hardware/gba/index.html. Nintendo JP's old per-model spec URL (/n08/hardware/gba/spec/) now returns 404, as does the Nintendo UK technical-data page that Wikipedia cites.

2. **Outline and front-panel shapes.** These come from Nintendo's own US design patent D452,280 S. It has orthographic FIG.1 (front), FIG.2 (rear), FIG.3 (top), FIG.4 (bottom) and FIG.5-6 (sides), downloaded from patentimages.storage.googleapis.com.
   - FIG.1 matches the official 144.5 x 82 aspect to within 0.25%, and its window rectangle (61.9 x 41.9) fits just outside the official 61.2 x 40.8 active area, so the drawing is to scale in the front plane.
   - The depth views (FIG.3 and FIG.4) are about 4.5% over-scale in depth, so I normalised them to 24.5 mm. The cartridge-slot depth then comes out at 7.5 mm, matching the cartridge thickness.

3. **Button, LED and screw positions (production).** These come from a 1200 DPI scan of a bare AGB-CPU-10 motherboard and its KiCad board outline (github.com/djedditt/kicad-agb-template, CC0).
   - **Scan calibration:** the scan reads 0.455% large, measured against the 1.50 mm cartridge-connector pitch. I corrected every scan value by x0.99547.
   - **Registration:** x_shell = (x_scan - 75.30)·0.99547 + 72.25. The board's six mounting holes are symmetric about x_scan = 75.30, and I assumed that line is the shell centreline. y_shell = y_scan·0.99547 - 0.88, a least-squares fit to the patent's button centres.
   - **Cross-check (board vs patent):** D-pad (-0.16, +0.07), Start (-0.16, -0.08), Select (-0.21, +0.02), A (+0.45, +0.15), B (+0.49, -0.17), LED (+0.58, +0.14). The board holes fall on the patent's six rear screws within 0.6 mm. Treat front-panel feature positions as ±0.5 mm and the outline as ±0.3 mm plus the drawing's own tolerance.
   - **Useful derived centres:** D-pad (19.95, 34.09), A (130.88, 31.92), B (117.94, 36.25), Start (29.49, 53.82), Select (29.44, 61.82), LED (118.14, 14.70), screen centre (72.25, 36.67), link port x 80.5, cartridge slot x 43.6-100.9.

4. **Internal notes for a handheld on this footprint.**
   - **Depth:** the full 24.5 mm depth exists only in a central band about 66 mm wide (x about 38-106). The grips thin to about 21 mm at x = 20 and about 16 mm at x = 10.
   - **Cartridge:** it occupies the rear 1.8-9.3 mm, top centre. It stands 35 mm tall and plugs into a 32-pin, 1.5 mm-pitch connector whose pads sit at y about 40-42.
   - **Battery bay:** the 2xAA box sits bottom centre on the back. The door is about 61 x 38 mm (x 42-103, y 41-78). It passes through a motherboard cut-out of about 63 x 32 mm (x 40.5-104.5, y 43.8 down to the bottom edge; narrowest clear width 57.3 mm).
   - **Motherboard:** the production board is 130.6 x 72.5 mm (x 6.9-137.5, y 3.4-75.9) and U-shaped.
   - **Shoulder switches:** the L and R tact switches sit near (15.9, 19.4) and (130.2, 17.5).
   - **Front-view clearance:** about 5-6 mm between the board edge and the outer silhouette on the long sides.

5. **Gaps and caveats.**
   - Speaker transducer diameter and the LCD module outline were not determined.
   - The cartridge envelope and the AA cell placement are marked ESTIMATE. They are inferred from the connector position, the door size and the cell spec, not measured. The "estimated-from-photo" tag on the cells is the closest available label; the arrangement comes from the rear photo and door size.
   - I did not use vendor IPS-kit or 3D-shell drawings. GitHub search was rate-limited, and the patent plus the board scan gave better-sourced data.
   - Silhouette notch handling: the patent shows small parting-line notches of about 1-1.5 mm at y ≈ 13.5-15.5 where the shoulder buttons meet the body. I smoothed them in the outline; a small residual kink remains at about (4.2-4.5, 12.9-14.2) and its mirror.
